heartbeat.title: Specific hooks beat generic urgency
heartbeat.body_html: The clearest pattern across August's winners is that a specific, emotionally precise hook outperforms broad urgency language. First-name personalisation paired with loss-framing, a founder curiosity angle in the welcome flow, and named pain points in winback all won their tests. We are now rolling that principle across subject and preview lines flow by flow, which is how small, banked wins compound into the per-email gains you saw this month.

narrative.html: Flows generated £36,524, up 34.1% on the prior month. Revenue per email delivered rose from £0.369 to £0.430, so the automations earned more from every send while volumes stayed steady.

Flows hold the most efficient per-email economics of any channel we run. At £0.430 per email versus £0.023 on campaigns, flows earn 18.7x more per send, which is why they carry 78% of email revenue off automated sends alone.

Campaigns added the second lever this month with 7 sends. They do a different job to the flows, reaching the whole list on a schedule, and together with the automations they lifted flow share of total store revenue to 8.1%, up from 7.4% in July.
Deliverability stayed healthy. Unsubscribes ran at 0.401% of delivered and spam complaints at 0.017%, well inside safe limits, so the added send volume is not straining list health.

monthly.title_sub: Flows delivered £36,524 in August, up 34.1% on July, and earned more per email than any other channel we run.

heartbeat.title: Specific beats generic
heartbeat.body_html: The clearest lesson from July's winners is that naming something concrete outperforms generic framing. The abandoned checkout win came from surfacing the named free bonus in the subject line rather than a generic benefit, and the browse abandon win replaced vague urgency with a time-specific expiry cue tied to the exact item viewed. When the message references something real to the reader, opens and revenue follow. We are now carrying that principle into the other flows as we keep testing.

narrative.html: Flows earned £27,244 this month, up 28.7% on June. Revenue per email delivered rose to £0.369 from £0.313, so each send is working harder, not just sending more.

Flows are the most efficient per-email channel we run. At £0.369 per email against £0.023 on campaigns, flows earn 16.0x more per email delivered. That is expected for triggered messages reaching people at the right moment, and it is why flows carry the programme.

Campaigns are the second lever we run alongside flows. Twelve campaigns went out in July, and together flows and campaigns split email revenue 60/40 in the flows' favour. Campaigns reach the whole list and keep the audience warm for the flows to convert.

Flows held 7.4% of total store revenue. On £366,574 in total store sales, flows accounted for 7.4%, up from 5.3% in June. Deliverability stayed healthy with unsubscribes at 0.312% and spam complaints at 0.018% of delivered.
